# Plan: SDK quickstart docs

## Onboarding flow
Step 1: clone the repo.
Step 2: install bun manually if not present.
Step 3: copy .env.example to .env and fill in 8 environment variables.
Step 4: run database migrations against your local Postgres.
Step 5: start the dev server.
Step 6: open the docs in a separate tab.
Step 7: register an API key by emailing the team.
Step 8: paste the key into your .env, restart the server, then make
your first SDK call.

No quickstart command, no hosted sandbox, no copy-pasteable curl example.

question.question:
D2 — Which time-to-first-SDK-call target should this review hold the quickstart plan to?
Project/branch/task: PLAN.md SDK quickstart docs on main, DX POLISH (docs scope held, no new product capabilities).
ELI10: The clock runs from 'developer opens the quickstart' to 'developer sees a successful response from their first SDK call and knows it worked.' Nothing has been measured. My estimate from the 8 declared steps: roughly 20-45 min of hands-on setup (bun, local Postgres, 8 env vars, migrations, server) [estimate], PLUS an unknown human wait at Step 7 (emailing for a key), which could be minutes or days [unknown]. That is Red Flag tier (>10 min, where industry rule of thumb says 50-70% abandon).
Peers (different boundaries, so compare choices, not stopwatch times): Stripe gives a self-serve sk_test_ key on signup plus a copy-paste curl in docs, and an in-docs Stripe Shell sandbox (docs.stripe.com/get-started/api-request). Resend: self-serve key in dashboard, then curl/Node/Python snippets (resend.com/docs/create-an-api-key). Twilio: 'build an app in minutes', SendGrid 'first email in under 10 minutes' (vendor-reported, not measured). None require cloning the vendor's server or running their DB.
Feasibility: Champion (<2 min) and Competitive (2-5 min) both need self-serve key issuance and/or a hosted sandbox. The plan explicitly has neither, and DX POLISH holds scope, so A and B mean expanding product scope (separate decisions). Within docs scope, polish can cut active setup time and make the key wait explicit, but cannot remove the wait.
Stakes if we pick wrong: an unreachable target makes every pass fail by design; too low a target hides the Step 7 blocker.
Recommendation: C because it is the only target reachable inside the held scope; the review will still flag the key wait and hosted options as out-of-scope opportunities.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: honest docs-scope target now vs. a faster target that requires product changes you haven't approved.

options.label: C) Current trajectory (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Reachable within held docs scope: ~20-45 min active setup [estimate] + Step 7 wait shown separately
✅ Passes measure doc clarity against the real journey, and the email-key blocker stays visible
❌ Still Red Flag tier; developers keep hitting an unbounded human wait before the first SDK call

options.label: A) Champion (< 2 min)
options.description:
✅ Matches Stripe/Resend-class onboarding where devs see a response almost immediately
✅ Biggest predicted adoption effect per the TTHW tiers (3-4x vs baseline, industry claim)
❌ Infeasible with docs only: needs self-serve keys plus hosted sandbox, which expands product scope

options.label: B) Competitive (2-5 min)
options.description:
✅ Baseline-tier experience that most hands-on developers would tolerate on first try
✅ Possibly reachable with self-serve keys and a copy-paste curl/SDK snippet against a hosted API
❌ Still blocked by email-for-key and local server setup; needs scope changes you have not approved

options.label: D) Tell me what's realistic
options.description:
✅ You supply the real constraint (e.g. key turnaround SLA, whether a hosted API exists)
✅ Lets the target reflect facts I could not find, since no outputs or timings were supplied
❌ Needs another round-trip and data the plan does not currently contain

question.question:
D2 — What time-to-first-SDK-call target should this quickstart plan aim for?
Project/branch/task: PLAN.md on main, SDK quickstart docs, DX POLISH.
ELI10: The clock: a hands-on developer starts at 'fresh clone, nothing installed or configured' and stops at 'first successful SDK call returns.' Today that path is 8 steps, including a local Postgres + migrations and a human email for the API key. Nothing has been measured. My ESTIMATE: 15-45+ min of hands-on work (wide because Postgres setup varies) PLUS an unmeasured wait on the email reply. That's Red Flag tier (>10 min, where 50-70% abandon).
Peer evidence (reported, not equivalent boundaries): Stripe issues test keys self-serve in ~30 seconds and shows copy-paste requests (docs.stripe.com/get-started); industry write-ups put good time-to-first-call under 2-5 min and say >10 min loses people. Those peers start from a hosted API, not a local server + DB, so I compare DX choices, not raw times.
Feasibility: Champion and Competitive both need self-serve keys or a sandbox, which are NEW capabilities outside DX POLISH. The docs alone can shrink the hands-on part but cannot remove the email wait.
Stakes if we pick wrong: an unreachable target forces scope creep later; a soft one lets a Red Flag journey ship as 'fine.'

options.label: Split target (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Hands-on steps target 5-10 min (Needs Work tier) via docs-only fixes; the key wait is measured and reported separately.
✅ Achievable inside DX POLISH with no new service, so the target is honest and testable.
❌ Total time stays Red Flag until key issuance changes, which this target explicitly does not fix.

options.label: Competitive (2-5 min)
options.description:
✅ Matches the peer baseline developers expect from hosted SDKs like Stripe or Resend.
✅ Would remove the biggest abandonment point, the email handoff for an API key.
❌ Not reachable in POLISH: needs self-serve keys or a sandbox, a scope change needing its own approval.

options.label: Champion (< 2 min)
options.description:
✅ Best adoption impact, roughly 3-4x per the TTHW benchmark tiers used in this review.
✅ Would make the first SDK call the magical moment instead of a chore after setup.
❌ Needs a hosted sandbox plus instant keys; far outside the supplied plan scope and DX POLISH.

options.label: Current trajectory
options.description:
✅ No change to the plan's journey; the review just documents the estimated 15-45+ min plus key wait.
✅ Zero added work for the docs authors beyond what the plan already lists.
❌ Accepts Red Flag tier, where most first-time developers give up before their first SDK call.
